findings.reason: §6's done-when claims the four reachable captures are the surface's real render, but the asset fork means the plan must name the authored-document owner and derive the set from it (as it already does for scripts via `authored_ui_module_paths`) rather than ship a parallel list that has already drifted.
findings.text: `_SPA_STYLESHEETS` is a hand-maintained 11-entry list whose owner is the authored document `docs/index.html` (12 `<link rel="stylesheet">`, including `/_ui/home.css` at line 16); the harness copy never references `docs/ui/home.css`, so a `file:` capture renders the fleet-home surface with none of its styling while the served SPA loads it — a capture taken through this path is not the render the surface actually produces

findings.reason: the honest change is an inline option on the renderer that already owns the document scaffold, which retires the parallel scaffold instead of letting it diverge; the plan's §6 must state that choice or its reason.
findings.text: the plan's §6 adds `write_file_spa_document` as a second SPA-document assembler beside `_render_spa_html`, which already renders the index the served SPA uses, and the plan justifies only why a second *harness* is avoided, never why the existing renderer cannot take an inline mode

findings.reason: adding the two owner citations to §6 turns a from-scratch document builder into an extension of the mechanisms that already own composition and rendering, which is the reuse the plan's §5 method commits it to.
findings.text: §6 says "inline the composed project state and every script into one document" without naming the mechanism that already composes state (`reckon/project_state.py::compose_project_state`) nor the renderer it re-scaffolds, so the plan's own reuse claim is narrower than the machinery its new path touches
